entities.summary: Alesso Baldovinetti was an Italian early Renaissance painter and draftsman born in Florence, Italy, around 1428. He was trained in the workshop of Fra Filippo Lippi and later worked in the court of the Medici family. Baldovinetti's style blended classical and contemporary elements, and he is known for his frescoes in the Palazzo Vecchio and the San Lorenzo monastery. His most famous work, the 'Last Judgment,' was completed in 1481. Baldovinetti's artistic influence can be seen in the works of Michelangelo and Raphael, who were both influenced by his style and technique. The artist's career was marked by a series of patronage agreements with powerful figures, including the Pope and the Medici family, which allowed him to travel extensively throughout Italy and Europe. Baldovinetti's legacy can be seen in the many artists who followed in his footsteps, including the Flemish masters and the Italian Renaissance painters. Despite his significant contributions to the art world, Baldovinetti's life was marked by a series of tragic events, including the death of his patrons and the decline of the Medici family's power. In 1499, Baldovinetti died at the age of 71, leaving behind a legacy that continues to inspire artists and art lovers to this day.
